reviews.pros:
Dropbox has apps for almost every operating system, including Windows, macOS, Android, iOS, Linux, and Kindle Fire. This makes it easy to access your files from any device, anywhere. You can also use Dropbox through a web browser if you don't have the app installed.

It has a variety of collaboration tools that allow you to share files and folders with other people and control who has access to them. You can also set expiration dates, password protection, and notifications for shared links. If you have a Business subscription, you can also create teams and manage permissions for your members.

Offerings for premium subscribers are solid, like 2TB of storage space, Smart Sync, Showcase, and Priority Support. These features let you store more files, save local drive space, present your work in a professional way, and get faster support from Dropbox.

Digital signatures can be added to documents through HelloSign, which is integrated with Dropbox. This can help you sign contracts, agreements, invoices, and other documents online securely and legally.

It integrates very well with applications with many popular services like Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, Slack, Zoom, Adobe Creative Cloud and more. This can help you work seamlessly across different apps and platforms without leaving Dropbox.

I like that this platform automatically backs up your files online and syncs them across all your devices. This can help you avoid data loss and keep your files up to date. You can also restore previous versions of your files or recover deleted files within 30 days (or longer if you have a paid plan).

Supports offline functionality for desktop and mobile apps. This means that you can access your files even when you don't have an internet connection. You can also mark specific files or folders offline, so they are available at any time.
reviews.cons:
Dropbox has poor storage limits for free users. The free plan only offers 2 GB of storage space, which is very low compared to other cloud storage services. If you need more space, you have to pay for a premium plan or refer others to join Dropbox.

Dropbox has some security weaknesses that may concern some users. For example, Dropbox doesn't offer end-to-end encryption for your files, which means they can be accessed by Dropbox or third parties under certain circumstances.

Its limited search feature which can make it difficult to find specific files or folders. For example, you can't search by file type, size, date modified, or content within files. You also can't use advanced operators like AND, OR, or NOT to refine your search.
reviews.overall: I have found Dropbox's cloud file sharing and storage service very effective, it is reliable and easy to use, offering many features and benefits for personal and professional use. It's especially useful for collaborating with others on projects and accessing your files from anywhere. However, it also has some drawbacks, such as low storage limits for free users, high prices for paid plans, security issues, and limited search functionality. Therefore, I would recommend Dropbox to anyone who needs a simple and flexible cloud storage solution that integrates well with other apps and services. However, I would also recommend users to compare Dropbox with other alternatives before making a final decision based on their needs and preferences.

reviews.title: Why is it the standard?

reviews.cons:

When being added to my company's dropbox, my new computer was rendered useless because it automatically tried to add ALL files to my computer's hard drive. It did this to several of my coworkers as well. Once you set up selective sync this isn't an issue, but actually GETTING selective sync set up when your computer is trying to download 1000+GB of info is a very frustrating experience. 

When using the dropbox app, every time you try to move files from a shared dropbox to your desktop (or whatever kind of local storage), it defaults to trying to remove the files from the dropbox for EVERYONE. Why is that the default? It prompts you every time that you are about to remove the files for everyone, but it doesn't give the option to adjust this setting. If you were clicking rapidly, it would be easy to miss and accidentally delete files. 

When uploading to other platforms, such as a DAM, you cannot upload directly from dropbox. You need to move the files to some kind of local storage, thus I am having to deal with this annoyance quite often. 

When viewing files on the dropbox in browser I find the file information inconsistent in how it is presented and downloading files is sometimes a pain. 

None of these issues are majorly problematic-- it just really makes the user experience less enjoyable. I've used other cloud-based storage platforms and found them to be a better user experience, for example Box.
